spec.title: herdr seat lifecycle

item.title: Testing seats in a scratch herdr

spec.purpose: Every process the factory runs is visible in a labelled herdr pane, comes up after the system that watches it, and is recovered or retired by a script, never by hand. This spec is the contract for seat.sh, monitors.sh and recover.sh, ported from bearings-v2 (~/tools/bearings-v2/bin) into this repo's herdr/ directory.

section.title: Bring-up order: system before agents

node.title: Monitoring and the system come up before any agent, so seats start hooked in
Bring-up DAG: herdr session, control plane, compaction-guard, monitor seat and log tab group, event log, then worker seats; seat.sh refuses a seat when any earlier node is down

section.mermaid: flowchart LR H[herdr session named per tier] --> CP[control plane up, health 200] CP --> G[compaction-guard doctor ok] G --> M[monitor seat + monitors tab group] M --> L[event log tail pane + queue pane] L --> S[seats: architect, workers, tester, reviewer, merger, player] S -- seat.sh --check each tick --> M
section.text: herdr/bin/bringup.sh runs the DAG in order and records seat.up 100 per node or stops at the first failure with a 500 record and a herdr notification. A seat started by any other path is detected by seat.sh --audit (it reads /proc for every agent process and compares flags against the role) and recorded as seat.stalled 500.

section.title: Workspaces, tabs, panes and labels
section.text: Workspace label = the repo name (coq), found by label, never by id (ids change on restart). One tab per seat, labelled with the seat name (worker-ba08). Tab group "monitors" holds fixed 3x3 grids: monitors-1 compaction watchers, monitors-2 loop, gate and log, monitors-3 shells. Pane labels: "<MODEL> - <effort> - <ticket> <seat>" for an agent, "MONITOR - <what>" for a watcher, "TOOL - <what>" for a tool, "test - <tool> <ticket>" for a suite, "<tool>-<tier>[-<ticket>]" for a tier server. Every pane carries HERDR_PANE_ID, HERDR_TAB_ID, HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH from herdr; a script that finds them unset refuses to start a process (Rule 18).

Layouts are JSON under herdr/layouts/ (grid plus slots: kind agent|monitor|viewer|tool, label, command), rendered into panes by seat.sh; their look is confirmed as wireframes in the SITREP before they are built (DEC-wireframe-gate).

section.title: How a seat comes up

node.title: seat.sh --ticket WO --role R: workspace by label, tab create, panes from layout, pane rename, markers unset, env exported, herdr agent start --kind --pane -- --model --effort --permission-mode --settings, guard bound, brief sent

section.text:
Order, each step a herdr command: workspace list (by label) or create; tab create --label --no-focus; pane split per layout slot; pane rename; pane run for monitor and tool slots; pane wait-output for the shell prompt; pane run "unset CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE_* CLAUDE_PID AI_AGENT; cd ; export COQ_SEAT COQ_TICKET COQ_ROLE_FILE COQ_WORKTREE RAIL_SURFACE"; herdr agent start --kind --pane

-- ; compaction-guard bind --session; seat.sh --check; herdr agent prompt "" without --wait. Codex seats get -m, reasoning effort and sandbox from the same role file; System One seats are not herdr agents, they are a tool pane of the player.

Idempotent: a rerun repairs (keeps a pane with the right label, relabels strays, splits what is missing). Cap: role max_seats; over cap posts 429 and the queue holds the ticket. A seat never starts with a missing status-line tap: the guard's sensor reads 0 without it (RSK-compaction-sensor).

section.title: Monitors tab group and wakeups

node.title: A waiting seat is woken through herdr on status change instead of idling

section.text: The monitor seat subscribes to herdr events (pane.agent_status_changed, pane.exited, workspace.closed) and tails events/. On a record it routes through routes.json and wakes the target with herdr agent prompt "<record id>" (one line). On blocked status it reads the pane (herdr agent read) and answers a known dialog or records 500. On events_lost it resubscribes and reconciles from session.snapshot. Owner notifications: herdr notification show "<code> <ticket> - <title>" for code 423 reaching the owner and for any 5xx; nothing else notifies (REQ-owner-notifications). Watcher log contract: one line on change only; ALERT prefix only for an owner decision.

section.title: Leases
section.text: Slots: treehouse leases keyed by ticket (slot.sh acquire --holder WO-ID), proven by treehouse status, released by slot.sh release which exits 5 if the pool still shows the holder. Tiers: the tier's server.json is the lease; a second start is refused. Tickets: work-order status in-progress plus the branch is the lease; the queue never hands a ticket out twice. Every lease has a ttl in config (herdr/config/leases.json) and the monitor releases an expired one, records seat.stalled 500, and wakes the queue.

section.title: Recovery

node.title: recover.sh [--check|--apply]: halt flag, herdr reachable, monitors grid, loop heartbeat, every seat seat.sh --check, down if the agent is gone, re-arm the guard per live pane, tickets report; notification at the end

section.text: Dead pane: herdr emits pane.exited; the pane stays with a shell; recovery is seat.sh --ticket again, which re-attaches by label and resumes the agent with the resume argv the integration hook reported (resume_agents_on_restore stays false so nothing resumes silently). Seat silent 900 s: resume up to 3 times, then 423 and seat down. Compaction after failure: SessionStart with source compact injects the checkpoint; the guard re-arms at the next turn end. A manual intervention is recorded with must_become naming the script that replaces it (P-016).

section.title: Cleanup and retirement

node.title: retire: agent send-keys esc, agent prompt /exit, poll agent get, answer the exit dialog, ctrl+c twice, close the emptied tab, release the slot, record seat.down 100

section.text: Cleanup is the monitor's responsibility and runs every tick: expired leases, finished tiers (uat after merge), stopped page servers, merged branches (work-order.sh cleanup), stale treehouse worktrees (treehouse prune, dry run then --yes for the disposable set only), test containers older than a day. Nothing is deleted that is leased, dirty or unmerged; those are recorded and left for the owner's card.

section.title: Breakglass and exemptions
section.text: Breakglass is a script (herdr/bin/breakglass.sh <seat> <minutes>): it lifts the guard freeze and the seat audit for that seat for that long, records GOV-5xx with the reason and the owner's card id, and re-arms itself. There is no other way to run something by hand. Exemptions live in herdr/config/exemptions.json (seat, rule, until UTC, card id); an exemption without a card id is invalid at lint.

section.title: Testing seats in a scratch herdr

node.title: Spike 11: scratch herdr session harness in Podman: start, create, assert, tear down

section.text: herdr server --session t-<id> runs headless; HERDR_SESSION or HERDR_SOCKET_PATH points the CLI at it; HERDR_CONFIG_PATH gives it a private config; teardown is session stop then session delete in a trap. The plugin registry is global, so plugin tests use plugin link and unlink. Panes in the scratch session get a stub claude on PATH so no real agent starts. Unset HERDR_PANE_ID and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH from the calling pane first or --current targets leak into the live session.

example.text: herdr pane rename wD3:p5 "test - bearings WO-20261010-ba08"; herdr pane run wD3:p5 "make test"; herdr pane wait-output wD3:p5 --regex 'tests: .* failed'.
seat.sh --ticket WO-20261010-ba08 --role worker rerun after a crash: same tab, same labels, agent resumed, guard re-bound, one seat.up record.
Monitor sees review.passed 201: herdr agent prompt merger "20261010T200101Z-201-k3f9q".
claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions typed by hand in a random pane.
example.why: No role, no guard, no audit; seat.sh --audit records it 500.
